NVDA.name: NVIDIA Corporation

thesis.short_term: Blackwell ramp and sovereign AI demand keep data-center revenue elevated; option skew remains bullish.
thesis.medium_term: Inference workload transition and cloud CapEx ROI questions are the key pivot — margin durability depends on software moat (CUDA, Dynamo).
thesis.long_term: Paradigm shift risk: algorithmic efficiency gains (e.g. on-device inference, ASIC competition) could erode the compute-intensive moat over 5-10y.

leading_indicators.name: CUDA Ecosystem Share
leading_indicators.description: Share of AI training/inference workloads on CUDA

leading_indicators.name: Blackwell Adoption
leading_indicators.description: Share of new hyperscaler deployments using Blackwell

bull_points: CUDA software moat remains structurally intact; >1M developers and rising.
Sovereign AI deals (Saudi, UAE, EU) add multi-year revenue visibility.
Networking (NVLink, Spectrum-X) becoming its own $10B+ franchise.
Blackwell uplift in perf/watt keeps hyperscaler CapEx ROI positive.
Automotive/robotics optionality priced at near-zero today.
bear_points: Customer concentration: top 4 hyperscalers ~40% of revenue; any CapEx pause hits hard.
Inference workloads can run on cheaper ASICs (Trainium, TPU, Groq) — long-term margin risk.
China export restrictions cut an addressable market and force margin-dilutive H20 variants.
AMD MI300X gaining meaningful traction in specific enterprise pockets.
Valuation premium leaves no room for any growth deceleration surprise.

PLTR.name: Palantir Technologies

thesis.short_term: Commercial US revenue and defense budget tailwinds sustain 30%+ growth; AIP bootcamps converting pipeline to TCV.
thesis.medium_term: Path to Rule-of-60 operating model hinges on commercial net retention and disciplined S&M leverage.
thesis.long_term: Category-defining data operating system for defense + large enterprises; moat is integration depth, not ML commodities.

leading_indicators.name: US Commercial Revenue YoY
leading_indicators.description: YoY growth of US commercial segment

leading_indicators.name: Net Dollar Retention
leading_indicators.description: Net revenue retention on existing customers

bull_points: Ontology + AIP is the only production-grade deployment layer for enterprise LLMs at scale.
Defense franchise (TITAN, Maven) creates multi-year backlog insulated from IT budget cycles.
Operating leverage: S&M expense line flat while revenue compounds 30%+.
Founder-led; long-dated option on commercial AI adoption curve.
bear_points: Valuation trades at 50-80x forward FCF, priced for perfection.
Concentrated customer base in government segment limits duration.
Share-based comp dilution remains elevated.
Competitors (Snowflake, Databricks, hyperscaler stacks) erode differentiation in vanilla use cases.

GOOGL.name: Alphabet Inc.

thesis.short_term: Search query volume remains resilient despite AI disruption; Gemini 3.0 launch closes product-gap narrative.
thesis.medium_term: Cloud (GCP) reaching structural profitability with AI training workload share; YouTube monetization has legs.
thesis.long_term: TPU silicon stack + Gemini models + Google-scale data form a vertical moat that's unique in big tech.

bull_points: TPU vertical stack gives Alphabet unit economics advantage vs GPU-dependent competitors.
YouTube Shorts monetization gap closing vs TikTok.
Waymo optionality essentially free at current valuation.
Capital return program (buybacks + dividend) supports floor.
bear_points: Antitrust remedies could force Search-default unbundling, hitting TAC economics.
ChatGPT-class assistants structurally reduce high-intent commercial queries.
CapEx step-up for AI infra compresses near-term FCF.
YouTube faces durable ad-market share pressure from Meta Reels.

MP.name: MP Materials

thesis.short_term: DoD magnet offtake contract provides revenue floor; NdPr pricing stabilizing off cycle lows.
thesis.medium_term: Stage-II (separation) + Stage-III (magnet production) execution is the key fundamental pivot — margin profile transforms once vertically integrated.
thesis.long_term: Only at-scale non-China rare earth supply chain; strategic premium expands as decoupling narrative persists.

bull_points: Strategic monopoly on US rare earth supply chain with DoD backing.
Vertical integration (mine → separation → magnet) triples revenue per ton of ore.
EV + defense + wind demand creates structural NdPr tailwind post-2026.
Tariff policy on Chinese magnets provides pricing umbrella.
bear_points: Chinese producers can dump supply to suppress pricing during political cycles.
Stage-III execution risk remains high; first magnet shipments slipping.
Capex-heavy business; debt funding dilutive.
NdPr demand elasticity poorly understood — substitution risk in EV motors.

NU.name: Nu Holdings

thesis.short_term: Brazil + Mexico customer adds driving ARPAC expansion; credit cost cycle stabilizing.
thesis.medium_term: Cross-sell into payroll lending and SME products lifts unit economics without proportional CAC.
thesis.long_term: LatAm's best-positioned consumer bank; Mexico/Colombia scale replicates Brazil playbook.

bull_points: Lowest-cost banking operator in LatAm; structural cost advantage compounds.
Mexico ramp repeating Brazil's vintage curve on accelerated timeline.
High-margin payroll lending ramp adds durable NII expansion.
Founder alignment; long-duration incentive structure.
bear_points: Brazilian macro (Selic, FX) drives meaningful earnings volatility.
Credit cycle risk elevated as LatAm consumer leverage rises.
Traditional LatAm banks (Itaú, Bradesco) aggressively cutting fees defensively.
Regulatory risk from BCB on interchange/credit card economics.

RCAT.name: Red Cat Holdings

thesis.short_term: SRR program of record execution and NDAA tailwinds drive backlog conversion.
thesis.medium_term: Teal 2/Black Widow platform becomes standard-issue US Army small UAS; international adoption adds optionality.
thesis.long_term: Category bet on small-UAS becoming as standard as night-vision in infantry kit — category TAM expansion is the bull case.

leading_indicators.name: Army SRR Delivery %
leading_indicators.description: Progress against SRR program of record units

bull_points: Only US-made small UAS with Blue UAS certification at scale — regulatory moat vs DJI.
Army SRR win validates platform; Marines + allied nations represent incremental TAM.
Ukraine war normalized small-UAS as essential warfighter kit globally.
Defense-tech M&A premium if scaled to $500M+ revenue.
bear_points: Small-cap; single-program risk if SRR schedule slips or is recompeted.
Gross margin still sub-20%, below defense-tech peer norms.
Cash burn with recurring equity raises dilutive.
Skydio + Anduril are well-funded competitors with deeper tech benches.

TSLA.name: Tesla Inc.

thesis.short_term: Delivery cadence and ASP mix are the short-term swing factors; Cybertruck ramp decelerating.
thesis.medium_term: FSD v13+ unsupervised adoption and robotaxi pilot economics will determine whether auto-gross-margin narrative shifts from cyclical to software-multiple.
thesis.long_term: Optimus + robotaxi: if either scales as Musk projects, current valuation is low. If neither does, the auto business alone does not justify today's multiple.

leading_indicators.name: Automotive Gross Margin (ex-credits)
leading_indicators.description: Core auto GM excluding regulatory credits

leading_indicators.name: FSD Take Rate
leading_indicators.description: Share of new vehicles with FSD purchase

bull_points: FSD unsupervised reaching inflection — software-margin revenue stream unlocks.
Optimus TAM is large enough to subsume the valuation if BOM economics work.
Energy storage (Megapack) is a $10B+ growing franchise ignored by sell-side.
Vertical integration (cells, silicon, dojo) yields cost structure peers cannot match.
bear_points: Core auto GM in mid-teens is commodity territory; BYD/Xiaomi price pressure durable.
Regulatory credit revenue fading faster than core GM expansion.
Key-person risk around Musk attention allocation (xAI, SpaceX, X, political).
Humanoid / robotaxi narratives frequently missed by meaningful timelines.

TSM.name: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing

thesis.short_term: AI-driven leading-edge demand (N3/N2) keeps utilization and ASPs elevated through 2026.
thesis.medium_term: Arizona/Japan/Germany fabs dilute margins near-term but derisk geopolitical concentration — CoWoS capacity is the binding constraint on AI accelerator TAM.
thesis.long_term: Unassailable process leadership at the leading edge; only Intel foundry + Samsung can theoretically compete and both lag 2+ nodes.

bull_points: Only company capable of manufacturing NVIDIA, AMD, Apple leading-edge silicon at scale.
CoWoS advanced packaging capacity is the binding supply constraint on AI hyperscale.
Arizona fab eases geopolitical discount over time.
Pricing power: ASP +10-15% per node transition with customer acceptance.
bear_points: Taiwan Strait geopolitical risk is the permanent overhang; valuation discount justified.
Overseas fabs structurally margin-dilutive vs Taiwan base.
Hyperscaler custom silicon (Trainium, TPU) still funnels to TSMC, but Samsung/Intel competition could stir pricing.
Cycle risk: AI capex pause would crater HPC utilization quickly.

UUUU.name: Energy Fuels

thesis.short_term: Uranium spot price + contracted volumes with DOE drive near-term revenue line; White Mesa mill utilization climbing.
thesis.medium_term: Rare earth / vanadium optionality at White Mesa diversifies vs pure-play uranium peers.
thesis.long_term: Structural US uranium supply shortage amid SMR build-out + reactor restarts supports multi-year pricing environment.

bull_points: Only fully-permitted, conventional US uranium mill operator — domestic supply premium.
Rare earth (NdPr) monazite processing at White Mesa adds a second cash-flow stream.
SMR reactor restarts (Palisades, Three Mile) create multi-decade demand tailwind.
Strong balance sheet; no meaningful debt.
bear_points: Uranium spot pricing remains volatile and Kazatomprom supply dominates.
Small-cap liquidity; sentiment-driven share-price swings.
Rare earth processing still early-stage and unproven at commercial scale.
Long production cycles mean revenue lags price signals meaningfully.

VOO.name: Vanguard S&P 500 ETF

thesis.short_term: Fed rate path + earnings breadth are the near-term drivers; AI concentration keeps top-10 weights elevated.
thesis.medium_term: Earnings growth vs multiple compression determines whether forward return matches historical 8-10%.
thesis.long_term: Broad-market S&P 500 exposure remains the default vehicle for durable compounded nominal growth of US corporate earnings.

bull_points: Cheapest total-cost-of-ownership S&P 500 exposure in ETF form (0.03% ER).
Earnings breadth broadening beyond Mag-7 supports next-leg returns.
Passive flow reflexivity continues to bid mega-cap weights.
Dollar-cost-averaging vehicle for core portfolio construction.
bear_points: Forward P/E elevated vs historical median; margin of safety low.
Concentration in AI-infra names creates hidden single-factor exposure.
Rising sovereign yields raise discount rate faster than earnings can absorb.
Passive-flow reflexivity works in reverse if outflows accelerate.

relative.target_metric: Forward index EPS × historical median P/E
